items: Base: Fable's recommended scene ("Nobody won this one", the regret question, "Every one of us", "Back then, you still can", "He's just the message").
Slower opening, your lines: "I know. And we both wish it hadn't happened that way." / "Well, it did. And here we are." / "Here we are. Nobody won this one, love."
Only data goes back, said plainly: "Not for him. Only data goes back. He's just the message." Then "That's the message" ties their regret to what travels.
Derek off-screen, positive, not the conclusion: "...I'd have that." / "Derek." / "Well. I would." Then "Come back tomorrow" as before, and voices start up behind the door.
No picture on the doorstep; the bus stays for the end. The whisper goes to the shut door, Maddie alone.

plan.h: The three drafts differ only in how the time machine comes in
items: 2D, she asks what he wants: "He didn't send you to say sorry." Maddie is caught out and confesses. ~62 s, the shortest.
2E, "Funny you should say that": she says "he can't take it back" and Maddie, embarrassed, admits he's working on it. ~66 s.
2F, regret first: the question and "Every one of us... not much use now" come before the machine, so it arrives as the answer. ~70 s.
Timings use the real pace of the voices already recorded for this scene (about 2.2 words a second); the doorstep in the cut today is 84 s of voice.
Pick 2D, 2E or 2F (or mix lines; note them).
The four questions in the Open questions tab.
Maddie's intro: a pick, now that your two line notes are answered below them.

replies.d1-1A-L4: Yes. Line 4 becomes: "Built all these world models and simulations to get you back, and nobody's home in any of them." I'll fold it into whichever intro draft you pick.
replies.d1-1A-L5: Yes. Line 5 becomes: "As it turns out, quantum physics is just stuff. Consciousness is the missing bit. That's why you lot are so special. [sad, regretful] He understands that now." It adds about 6 s, so 1A runs about 26 s against the 20 s target; it's worth it, as it's the line the doorstep's "nobody won" stands on.
